problem: Which integral gives the area of the finite region bounded between $y={x}^{2}-5$ and $y=4x?$
worked_solution:
First, let's draw a sketch of the two functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013841/assets/b25bee7ef7257a5611d708eb65b3c8b453b230ad6d2e9289f6cb40dffba89277.png)

*(Note: Figure not drawn to scale)*

Now, we want to determine the limits of integration. To do this, we equate the two functions and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & ={x}^{2}-5 \\ {x}^{2}-4x-5 & =0 \\ (x+1)(x-5) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we need to integrate from $x=-1$ to $x=5.$

To determine which is the lower function and which is the upper, let's draw our vertical arrow.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013841/assets/bf79cec9c1ede4a95b3e20415fbf37224ca8616426e8530043fa4a4b54780bab.png)

The vertical line 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y={x}^{2}-5,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=4x.$

Therefore, the integral that gives our area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{-1}^{5}[\,(\text{upper function})-(\text{lower function})\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{5}[\,(4x)-({x}^{2}-5)\,]\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{5}(-{x}^{2}+4x+5)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{5}(5+4x-{x}^{2})\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
